THE FAITHFUL PRINCE

Bahrdmgor, p. 23.—This tale is a variant in a way of a popular story
published in the Panjab in various forms in the vernacular, under the
title of the Story of Bahramgor and the Fairy Hasan Béno. The person
meant is no doubt Bahramgor, the Sassanian King of Persia, known to
the Greeks as Varanes V., who reigned 420-438 a.D. The modern
stories, highly coloured with local folklore, represent the well-known
tale in India—through the Persian—of Bahrdmgor and Dilérdm.
Bahramgor was said to have been killed while hunting the wild ass (gor),
by jumping into a pool after it, when both quarry and huntsman dis-
appeared for ever. He is said to be the father of Persian poetry.
